# LightRAG Storage Options — Technical Report

**Report status: PARTIAL**  
The research execution ended `partial_or_incomplete`: step 1 completed; steps 2 and 3 hit tool-round limits (partial); step 4 was blocked and never ran. This report synthesizes the evidence actually collected, labels each claim, and discloses exactly what remains unverified. It does **not** imply the research is complete.

---

## 1. Official documentation and repository

| Item | Finding | Evidence |
|------|---------|----------|
| Official documentation URL | `https://lightrag.github.io/` — reachable (HTTP 200, `text/html`); page title "LightRAG", description "LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation" | [call-04181898](https://lightrag.github.io/), [call-966efac9](https://lightrag.github.io/) |
| Official GitHub repository | `https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag` (HKUDS/LightRAG) | [call-0e1ecf21](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag), [call-e9f41fad](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag) |
| Repository metadata | MIT license; ~40.5k stars; ~5.7k forks; 10,873 commits; associated with EMNLP2025 paper arXiv:2410.05779 | [call-aa2fac7a](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag), [call-b41807d6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hkuds/lightrag/main/README.md) |

**Assessment:** Claims `step_1:claim_1`, `step_1:claim_2`, and `step_1:claim_3` are **supported** by official sources.

---

## 2. Supported storage backends (evidence status: partial)

LightRAG defines four storage roles. The following is drawn from step-2 evidence citing `docs/ProgramingWithCore.md` and `docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md`. Because step 2 hit its tool-round limit, **claim `step_2:claim_5` (each backend claim cross-checked against official documentation) is unsupported**; treat the backend list as **partially supported**.

| Storage role | Purpose (per docs) | Default (demo/dev only) | Production-capable unified backends | Specialized / role-specific backends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `KV_STORAGE` | LLM response cache, text chunks, document information | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL (`PGKVStorage`), MongoDB, OpenSearch | — |
| `VECTOR_STORAGE` | Entity, relation, and chunk embedding vectors | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL (`PGVectorStorage`) | Milvus, Qdrant |
| `GRAPH_STORAGE` | Entity–relation graph | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL (`PGGraphStorage`, via Apache AGE) | Neo4j, Memgraph |
| `DOC_STATUS_STORAGE` | Document indexing status | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL, MongoDB, OpenSearch | — |

Sources: [call-faa610e5](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md), [call-50201106](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md), [call-1fc3d299](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md), [call-efcb1bae](https://www.prompts.brightcoding.dev/blog/lightrag-the-revolutionary-dual-level-graph-rag-system), [call-ff664c6a](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag).

**Key documented caveat:** the default in-memory/file-persisted stores are suitable only for small-scale testing and evaluation, **not** production [call-1fc3d299].

---

## 3. Differences between the available storage options

This section is **reasoned synthesis** from the evidence above, not a direct quote from docs.

| Dimension | In-memory / file (default) | Unified backend (PostgreSQL / MongoDB / OpenSearch) | Specialized backends (Milvus/Qdrant, Neo4j/Memgraph) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scope | All four roles in one lightweight store | All four roles in one operational database | One role only (vector or graph) |
| Query model | Simple key/value lookups | SQL (PostgreSQL) or document/query language | Vector similarity (Milvus/Qdrant); Cypher (Neo4j/Memgraph) |
| Durability / backup | Limited (file-persisted only) | Production-grade backup, replication, ACID (PostgreSQL) | Varies by product; separate operational footprint |
| Operational overhead | None | Single database to operate | Multiple databases to operate and keep in sync |
| Production suitability | No | Yes — PostgreSQL explicitly recommended for production | Yes for the specific role, but adds infra complexity |
| Notable dependency | None | PostgreSQL graph role requires Apache AGE extension | None beyond the product itself |

**Conflict to note:** Some secondary summaries present MongoDB and OpenSearch as equivalent unified production options alongside PostgreSQL [call-efcb1bae, call-ff664c6a], while the Railway deployment summary and step-3 evidence focus on PostgreSQL as *the* recommended production backend [call-21bdb92b, call-93b1c585]. I could not independently verify MongoDB/OpenSearch implementation details against the official docs within the evidence boundary.

---

## 4. Is PostgreSQL / Neon suitable?

### PostgreSQL — supported as suitable, with conditions

- PostgreSQL is recommended for production and can serve all four storage roles on its own [call-21bdb92b](https://railway.com/deploy/lightrag-knowledge-graph-rag-postgres-production--lightrag-postgres-graph-rag), [call-93b1c585](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md).
- Concrete storage classes exist: `PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGGraphStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage` [call-d60bc60f](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/examples/lightrag_gemini_postgres_demo.py).
- **Graph storage dependency:** `PGGraphStorage` is built on the Apache AGE PostgreSQL extension. A stock PostgreSQL image **cannot** provide graph storage without AGE [call-a4b0432f](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/DockerDeployment.md). The referenced Docker image `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` bundles Apache AGE + pgvector [call-a4b0432f].
- Azure documentation confirms Apache AGE adds graph (openCypher) capabilities to PostgreSQL [call-2874ab74](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/azure-ai/generative-ai-age-overview).

### Neon — partially supported; graph role unverified

- Neon is a serverless PostgreSQL service, described as 100% Postgres-compatible, and supports the `pgvector` extension for vector similarity search [call-39908b6b](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/neon-serverless-postgres-announces-native-190800299.html), [call-b671acde](https://neon.com/docs/extensions/pgvector).
- **Critical gap:** the evidence explicitly states there are **no specific details about Neon's support for the Apache AGE extension** [call-2874ab74]. Since `PGGraphStorage` requires AGE, Neon's suitability for the **graph storage role is unverified**. Neon may be suitable for KV, vector, and document-status storage (standard Postgres + pgvector), but using it for graph storage would require confirmation that AGE can be installed/enabled on Neon, or pairing Neon with a dedicated graph database.

**Verdict:** PostgreSQL (self-managed or managed, with pgvector + Apache AGE) is a suitable, documented production setup. Neon is plausibly suitable for three of four roles but **not confirmed** for the graph role.

---

## 5. Compatibility limitations and configuration considerations

### Configuration (partially supported)
Environment variables identified for PostgreSQL configuration:
- `POSTGRES_HOST`, `POSTGRES_PORT`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DATABASE`
- `LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE=PGKVStorage`, `LIGHTRAG_VECTOR_STORAGE=PGVectorStorage`, `LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE=PGGraphStorage` [call-d60bc60f](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/examples/lightrag_gemini_postgres_demo.py), [call-93b1c585](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md)

### Known limitations / caveats (partially supported)
1. Default in-memory/file stores are not production-suitable [call-1fc3d299].
2. Stock PostgreSQL lacks graph storage without Apache AGE [call-a4b0432f].
3. Apache AGE support on Neon is not evidenced [call-2874ab74].
4. Official Docker image status: a feature request exists; sources do not confirm an official image has been published [call-cc9a1549](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/1417).
5. Cross-check of every backend claim against official docs was not completed (step-2 limit) — `step_2:claim_5` unsupported.

---

## 6. Recommended production storage architecture (reasoned recommendation)

**Primary recommendation:** Single PostgreSQL instance (self-hosted or managed, e.g., RDS / Cloud SQL) running the `pgvector` and `apache/age` extensions, serving all four LightRAG storage roles:
- `KV_STORAGE` → `PGKVStorage`
- `VECTOR_STORAGE` → `PGVectorStorage` (pgvector)
- `GRAPH_STORAGE` → `PGGraphStorage` (Apache AGE)
- `DOC_STATUS_STORAGE` → `PGDocStatusStorage`

Configure via the environment variables above; use connection pooling, automated backups, and monitoring. Use the `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` image pattern (or equivalent) if containerizing [call-a4b0432f].

**If Neon is required:** Use Neon for KV, vector, and document-status storage (standard Postgres + pgvector). For the graph role, either (a) confirm Apache AGE is available on Neon before committing, or (b) run a dedicated graph database (Neo4j or Memgraph) for `GRAPH_STORAGE` and keep Neon for the other three roles. Do not assume Neon supports `PGGraphStorage` without verification.

**Do not use** the default in-memory/file-persisted storage in production.

---

## 4. Requirement 3 — Differences between available storage options

**Documented facts:**
- Default stores (`NetworkX`, `NanoVectorDB`, JSON files) use in-memory databases and local file persistence; documentation is explicit that these are for development and debugging, **not production** (call-68d45e48 observations; call-cb298109; call-9c4393a6).
- PostgreSQL can serve all four roles with one instance: `PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGGraphStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage`. Requires `pgvector` and Apache AGE extensions (call-57f909ea; call-23d05e40; call-cb298109).
- OpenSearch offers native k-NN vector search, full-text search, and horizontal scalability without cloud-only restrictions; requires OpenSearch 3.x+ with k-NN plugin (call-9c4393a6).
- MongoDB: local Community Edition (e.g., bundled Docker) supports KV/graph/doc-status but **not** `MongoVectorDBStorage`; vector requires MongoDB Atlas Search/Vector Search (call-9c4393a6).
- Redis is supported for KV only; persistence and memory usage must be configured carefully (call-9c4393a6).
- Specialized engines: Milvus/Qdrant for vector at scale; Neo4j/Memgraph for native graph traversal (call-8a6f1a23; call-9c4393a6).

**Reasoned comparison:**
- **Operational simplicity:** Single PostgreSQL instance < OpenSearch single backend < split PostgreSQL + specialized vector/graph engines.
- **Consistency:** PostgreSQL offers ACID for KV and doc-status; this is implied by the technology, not explicitly guaranteed in the excerpts (step_3:claim_3 = unsupported).
- **Scale:** pgvector guidance suggests it fits existing PostgreSQL with fewer than ~50M vectors; Milvus/Qdrant/Weaviate are suggested for new projects at 10–100M vectors (call-0b10ba97 — partly third-party). OpenSearch is proposed as a scalable, cost-effective open-source alternative for large datasets (call-0b10ba97).
- **Graph capability:** PostgreSQL-backed graph relies on LightRAG's own graph implementation over Postgres (via Apache AGE), not a native graph engine; Neo4j/Memgraph provide native traversal at the cost of extra infrastructure (call-8a6f1a23 step_6 answer).

**Conflicts noted:** One summary states Redis is "recommended for production deployment" for KV (call-9c4393a6), while the dominant recommendation is PostgreSQL for all four roles in production. These are not contradictory if read as "Redis can be production-grade for the KV role" versus "PostgreSQL is the recommended single-backend production choice." I treat them as complementary, not conflicting.

- **PostgreSQL (all four roles):** Simplest deployment; one backup/restore and monitoring domain; ACID consistency for KV and doc-status; pgvector provides competent vector search without a separate system. - **MongoDB:** Native KV and vector support with document-model flexibility. Trade-off: vector requires Atlas; not a clean single-backend answer for all roles.
- **OpenSearch:** Unified single backend for all four roles; horizontal scalability. Trade-off: heavier operational footprint than PostgreSQL; different consistency characteristics.

- **Neo4j/Memgraph (graph):** Native graph traversal. Trade-off: extra infrastructure, licensing (Neo4j), consistency boundaries with Postgres.

AI Agent (LightRAG) ──► Managed PostgreSQL (primary)

                        ├─ Vector storage (PGVectorStorage + pgvector)
                        ├─ Graph storage (PGGraphStorage + Apache AGE)

| Dimension | Default / file-backed (Json/NanoVectorDB/NetworkX) | Redis | PostgreSQL (unified) | Specialized (Milvus/Qdrant/Faiss; Neo4j/Memgraph) |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------|-------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| Persistence | Local file persistence | In-memory / Redis persistence | Durable, ACID (Postgres) | Varies by product |
| Intended scale | Small-scale testing / debugging only | Production | Production; single DB for all four roles | Production; high-scale specialized workloads |
| Extensions required | None | Redis server | `pgvector` (vector) + Apache AGE (graph) | Separate product + client libs |
| Operational complexity | Lowest | Medium | Lowest for unified setup (one DB) | Highest (multiple systems) |
| Evidence-quoted guidance | “explicit … for development and debugging, not production” (Railway) | Production KV/doc-status | Recommended for production with large datasets; can serve all four types on its own | Recommended for vector (Milvus/Qdrant/Faiss) and graph (Neo4j/Memgraph) |

**Key trade-offs captured in evidence:**
- Default file-backed stores are explicitly **not for production** [Railway guide via call-95225fa6-b1a3-4912-bd98-9615f645c1b0].
- PostgreSQL is the simplest production path because one database covers KV, vector (pgvector), graph (Apache AGE), and doc-status — “no Neo4j, Milvus, or Redis to run separately” [Railway guide].
- Specialized stores (Milvus/Qdrant for vector; Neo4j/Memgraph for graph) are offered for cases where a dedicated engine is preferred, at the cost of running additional infrastructure [LightRAG-API-Server.md via call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c; DEV.to via call-125f3740-ef94-496c-8536-23532cc72d8c].
- No benchmark numbers (latency, throughput, ingest rate) are present in the evidence, so performance comparisons are **qualitative only**.

## 4. Is PostgreSQL / Neon suitable?

### PostgreSQL — supported and recommended
**Confirmed by multiple sources.** LightRAG provides `PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGGraphStorage`/`PGTableGraphStorage`, and `PGDocStatusStorage`, and the documentation recommends PostgreSQL for production deployments with large datasets because it can serve all four storage types on its own [call-95225fa6-b1a3-4912-bd98-9615f645c1b0][call-55a8eb85-9196-4913-bb0a-04354d60ea8c][call-3aa4dcd9-4e89-490e-8240-461f44eab0f8].

The Railway production template runs `ghcr.io/hkuds/lightrag` against a PostgreSQL service built with **pgvector** and **Apache AGE** extensions, pointing all four LightRAG storage roles at Postgres via `LIGHTRAG__STORAGE` variables [call-95225fa6-b1a3-4912-bd98-9615f645c1b0][call-2307c180-8010-46f8-869b-98feb306688e][call-52464c71-2bc8-466b-a311-35f810879bcb].

**Configuration requirements (PostgreSQL):**
- Storage selection: `LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE`, `LIGHTRAG_VECTOR_STORAGE`, `LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE`, `LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS_STORAGE` (e.g., `PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGTableGraphStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage`) [call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c][call-16e396f0-4214-4de1-9b69-68311a4752e3][call-042af0fb-1837-4484-a350-6df9aa58598b].
- Postgres connection: `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DATABASE`, plus `POSTGRES_HOST` and `POSTGRES_PORT` [call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c][call-042af0fb-1837-4484-a350-6df9aa58598b]. Example demo values: host `localhost`, port `5432`, user `admin`, password `admin` [call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c][call-16e396f0-4214-4de1-9b69-68311a4752e3].
- Extensions: `pgvector` for vector storage; **Apache AGE is required for graph storage** (`PGGraphStorage` relies on AGE) — not plain PostgreSQL [call-2307c180-8010-46f8-869b-98feb306688e][call-52464c71-2bc8-466b-a311-35f810879bcb][call-1a2e4769-1c51-4bc5-a6cf-73af04f6fbf8].
- `make env-storage` is used to configure storage; PostgreSQL/Milvus/Memgraph can be run locally via Docker [call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c].

### Neon — not confirmed as a LightRAG backend
The evidence contains general information about Neon (cloud-native PostgreSQL, separated pageserver/safekeeper storage, WAL via safekeepers) [call-43459066-c202-4bc7-8849-ca407255e00d], but **no source states that LightRAG officially supports Neon**, and no LightRAG-specific Neon configuration is documented. Neon is PostgreSQL-compatible, so a connection *might* work, but the evidence does not confirm that the required extensions (especially **Apache AGE** for graph storage) are available on Neon. → **Neon suitability for LightRAG is unverified; do not recommend it for graph storage without confirmation.**

## 6. Recommended production storage architecture (reasoned recommendation)

> This recommendation is **reasoned from the evidence**, not a verbatim architecture published by LightRAG. It should be validated against the LightRAG version you deploy.

### Default recommendation: unified PostgreSQL backend
For a production AI agent, start with **one PostgreSQL instance serving all four LightRAG storage roles**:

- KV: `PGKVStorage`
- Vector: `PGVectorStorage` (requires `pgvector`)
- Graph: `PGTableGraphStorage` / `PGGraphStorage` (requires Apache AGE; verify class name for your version)
- Document status: `PGDocStatusStorage`

Set:
```
LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE=PGKVStorage
LIGHTRAG_VECTOR_STORAGE=PGVectorStorage
LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE=PGTableGraphStorage   # verify PGGraphStorage vs PGTableGraphStorage
LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS_STORAGE=PGDocStatusStorage
POSTGRES_HOST=... POSTGRES_PORT=5432 POSTGRES_USER=... POSTGRES_PASSWORD=... POSTGRES_DATABASE=...
```

**Rationale (evidence-based):**
- Officially recommended for production with large datasets; single DB covers all four roles [call-95225fa6-b1a3-4912-bd98-9615f645c1b0][call-55a8eb85-9196-4913-bb0a-04354d60ea8c].
- Operationally simplest: no separate Neo4j, Milvus, Qdrant, or Redis cluster [Railway guide via call-95225fa6-b1a3-4912-bd98-9615f645c1b0].
- ACID transactions via PostgreSQL/Apache AGE [call-52464c71-2bc8-466b-a311-35f810879bcb].

### When to diverge (hybrid / specialized)
If a single Postgres instance becomes a bottleneck, the evidence supports splitting roles:
- KV + doc-status: Redis (`RedisKVStorage`, `RedisDocStatusStorage`) or keep Postgres.
- Vector: Milvus / Qdrant / Faiss (Milvus needs GPU consideration).
- Graph: Neo4j or Memgraph (dedicated graph engines), instead of PostgreSQL+AGE.

The API-Server’s own “recommended storage choices” example mixes `PGKVStorage` + `PGDocStatusStorage` with `MilvusVectorDBStorage` and `MemgraphStorage`, showing a hybrid pattern is documented [call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c][call-16e396f0-4214-4de1-9b69-68311a4752e3]. This increases operational complexity, so adopt only if specific scale or performance requirements justify it.

### Neon
Do **not** select Neon as the graph backend based on current evidence: Apache AGE availability on Neon is unconfirmed. If you want to use Neon for KV/vector/doc-status via `pgvector`, treat it as experimental and verify extension support first.

### Operational guardrails (from evidence)
- Set storage env vars **before first launch**; run `make env-storage`.
- Use Docker Compose for local Postgres (+ Milvus/Memgraph if hybrid) [call-c3d9e4cf-5364-469d-a256-b02f3f0c1d1c].
- Back up before LightRAG upgrades; expect possible long downtimes [issue #2255 via call-2307c180-8010-46f8-869b-98feb306688e].
- Confirm PostgreSQL version supports Apache AGE (evidence: up to v16) before provisioning.

## 3. Section 2 — Supported storage backends

LightRAG requires four storage types: **KVStorage** (caching LLM responses and text chunks), **VectorStorage** (embedding vectors), **GraphStorage** (entity–relation graphs), and **DocStatusStorage** (document indexing status) [call-78935ce9; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md]. The default stores are in-memory databases with local file persistence, suitable only for small-scale testing/evaluation, not production [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc].

### 3.1 Key-value storage backends

- `JsonKVStorage` (default) [call-35215f23 observation via dev.to]

MongoDB and OpenSearch are the other single-backend production options; Milvus/Qdrant (vector) and Neo4j/Memgraph (graph) are specialized alternatives [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc] [call-31224b71].

## 4. Section 3 — Differences between available storage options

The boundary provides **directional** differences but not a full comparative matrix.

| Dimension | What the boundary states | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| KV role | Caches LLM responses and text chunks | [call-78935ce9] |
| KV options | JSON / PostgreSQL / Redis named for KV | [call-31224b71] |
| Vector role | Embedding vectors | [call-78935ce9] |
| Vector options | FAISS, Chroma, Milvus named; PG vector supports HNSW and IVFFlat indexes (`POSTGRES_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPE`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_M`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_EF`, `POSTGRES_IVFFLAT_LISTS`) | [call-31224b71] [call-2c556838] |
| Graph role | Entity–relation graphs | [call-78935ce9] |
| Graph options | Neo4j and PostgreSQL AGE named; Apache AGE is **required** for `PGGraphStorage` — a stock PostgreSQL image cannot provide it; AGE supports openCypher | [call-31224b71] [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09] |
| Doc-status role | Document indexing status | [call-78935ce9] |
| Production suitability | Default in-memory + local file persistence = small-scale testing only; PostgreSQL recommended for production; specialized DBs (Milvus/Qdrant vector, Neo4j/Memgraph graph) for workloads needing them | [call-7876a2cc] [call-c21ffffd] [call-31224b71] |

**Conflicts/omissions:** Chroma appears as a vector option in one summary [call-31224b71] but is absent from the list tied to the official docs [call-38fa5da4]. No per-backend trade-off detail (e.g., Neo4j vs Memgraph vs NetworkX) is provided.

---

## 5. Section 4 — PostgreSQL / Neon suitability

### 5.1 PostgreSQL support status
**Supported.** PostgreSQL is an officially recommended production backend serving all four storage roles [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09] [call-3002da7b] [call-c21ffffd]. For graph storage it uses `PGGraphStorage`, which requires **pgvector + Apache AGE**; the official Docker image referenced is `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` (bundles Apache AGE and pgvector), and `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` is suggested for non-graph storage [call-f64c3f09; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/DockerDeployment.md]. A Railway production template uses PostgreSQL for all four storage roles and is described as production-grade [call-69bb6213; https://railway.com/deploy/lightrag-knowledge-graph-rag-postgres-production--lightrag-postgres-graph-rag].

### 5.2 Neon compatibility
**Partially supported — compatibility not confirmed.**
- Neon is a serverless PostgreSQL provider; the boundary confirms Neon supports PostgreSQL and extensions such as `pg_embedding` for vector search [call-3138b8ec] [call-209c58b4] [call-cc7fef0c; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/azure-ai/generative-ai-age-overview].
- **Apache AGE support on Neon is not confirmed.** Three sources state Neon does **not explicitly mention** Apache AGE and that it is unknown whether Neon serverless PostgreSQL supports AGE [call-3138b8ec] [call-209c58b4] [call-cc7fef0c]. One source states Neon supports extensions "including Apache AGE" but then concedes there is no specific LightRAG-on-serverless information [call-9c56041b].
- Because `PGGraphStorage` depends on Apache AGE, **Neon cannot be confirmed as a drop-in replacement for the full four-role PostgreSQL setup** unless AGE availability on Neon is verified.

### 5.3 Production suitability evaluation
**Partially supported.** Self-hosted or managed PostgreSQL with pgvector + Apache AGE is supported for production (Railway template, official Docker image) [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09]. Neon serverless suitability is **uncertain** due to the unconfirmed AGE dependency for graph storage.

---

## 6. Section 5 — Compatibility limitations and configuration considerations

### 6.1 Compatibility limitations
**Partially supported (not exhaustive).**
- **Stock PostgreSQL is insufficient for graph storage:** Apache AGE extension is required; a stock PostgreSQL image cannot provide `PGGraphStorage` [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09].
- **Mixed-stack issue:** GitHub issue #860 reports that using Milvus + Neo4j + PostgreSQL together leaves the `lightrag_doc_chunks` table empty after document processing [call-b75d434f; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/860].
- **MongoDB vector storage:** reported as available only on MongoDB Atlas Cloud [call-35215f23 observation via dev.to].
- The boundary explicitly states there is **no definitive answer on the compatibility limitations of all mentioned storage backends** [call-c21ffffd].

### 6.2 Configuration requirements
**Supported.** Environment variables for PostgreSQL storage selection:
- `LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE=PGKVStorage`
- `LIGHTRAG_VECTOR_STORAGE=PGVectorStorage`
- `LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE=PGGraphStorage`
- `LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS_STORAGE=PGDocStatusStorage`
- PostgreSQL connection: `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DATABASE`, `POSTGRES_HOST`, `POSTGRES_PORT`; additional `PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `PGCLIENTENCODING`, `PGTARGE...` (truncated) [call-3002da7b; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md].

Neon/PostgreSQL-specific additions reported:
- `POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `POSTGRES_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPE`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_M`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_EF`, `POSTGRES_IVFFLAT_LISTS`; vector index types HNSW and IVFFlat; default PostgreSQL workspace is `default` [call-2c556838].

### 6.3 Version constraints / dependencies
**Partially supported.** Docker images reference PostgreSQL 18 (`pg18`): `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` and `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` [call-f64c3f09]. One source states **no specific version constraints** are provided [call-c8463c9d]. No complete version matrix exists in the boundary.

---

## 7. Section 6 — Production storage architecture recommendation

> This recommendation is **reasoned from the evidence**, not an official LightRAG publication. It is labeled provisional because Neon/AGE compatibility and full backend compatibility were not verified.

### Recommended architecture (single-backend, simplest production path)

| Role | Backend | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| KV | `PGKVStorage` | PostgreSQL serves all four roles; official production recommendation [call-918fd425] [call-c21ffffd]. |
| Vector | `PGVectorStorage` (pgvector, HNSW or IVFFlat) | Avoids operating a separate vector DB; index type tunable via env vars [call-2c556838]. |
| Graph | `PGGraphStorage` (PostgreSQL + Apache AGE + pgvector) | Required extension stack; official Docker image `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` bundles it [call-f64c3f09]. |
| Doc status | `PGDocStatusStorage` | Same PostgreSQL instance [call-3002da7b]. |

**Deployment:** Run PostgreSQL with pgvector and Apache AGE preloaded (e.g., the referenced Docker image or equivalent managed PostgreSQL where AGE can be installed). Configure via the environment variables in Section 6.2. Do **not** use the default in-memory/Json/Nano/NetworkX stores in production [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc].

### Neon-specific guidance
Neon is **not recommended as the sole production backend until Apache AGE support is confirmed**, because `PGGraphStorage` depends on AGE. If Neon is desired for KV/vector/doc-status (it supports PostgreSQL and `pg_embedding`), pair it with a separate graph backend (Neo4j or Memgraph) — but note the mixed-stack issue in GitHub issue #860 [call-b75d434f], which suggests testing a combined stack thoroughly or avoiding it.

### Alternative (specialized) architecture
If vector or graph workloads are large/specialized: PostgreSQL for KV + doc status; Milvus or Qdrant for vector; Neo4j or Memgraph for graph [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc]. This increases operational complexity and is only justified when single-backend PostgreSQL is insufficient.

### Key configuration cautions
1. Install/preload Apache AGE (graph) and pgvector (vector) on PostgreSQL; stock PostgreSQL is not enough for graph [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09].
2. Avoid the Milvus + Neo4j + PostgreSQL combination without verifying the `lightrag_doc_chunks` issue (#860) is resolved [call-b75d434f].
3. MongoDB vector storage is Atlas Cloud-only per the boundary [call-35215f23 observation].
4. No full version matrix is available; pin to tested images (e.g., pg18-based) rather than assuming latest compatibility [call-f64c3f09] [call-c8463c9d].
